name: Clean Architecture
description: Uncle Bob's Clean Architecture — concentric layers with the dependency rule. Entities at the center, use cases orchestrate, adapters translate.

rules.name: Dependency Rule
rules.instruction: Source code dependencies point inward only. Inner layers must never reference outer layers. The dependency direction is: frameworks → adapters → use cases → entities.

rules.name: Entities Encapsulate Business Rules
rules.instruction: Entities contain enterprise-wide business rules and critical data. They have no knowledge of use cases, databases, or UI. They are the most stable layer.

rules.name: Use Cases Orchestrate
rules.instruction: Use cases contain application-specific business rules. Each use case is a single operation that orchestrates entities and data flow. One use case per file.

rules.name: Interface Adapters Translate
rules.instruction: Adapters convert data between the format most convenient for use cases and the format required by external systems (DB, web, UI). No business logic in adapters.

rules.name: Frameworks are Details
rules.instruction: Frameworks and drivers occupy the outermost layer. The application does not depend on any framework — frameworks are pluggable. Database choice, web framework, and UI toolkit are all details.

rules.name: Crossing Boundaries with Interfaces
rules.instruction: When control flow crosses a boundary inward-to-outward, use dependency inversion: define an interface in the inner layer and implement it in the outer layer.

rules.name: Data Transfer Objects at Boundaries
rules.instruction: Data that crosses layer boundaries uses simple DTOs or value objects. Never pass entity objects directly to outer layers — map them at the boundary.

rules.name: Testability by Design
rules.instruction: Every layer is independently testable. Use cases are tested without UI, database, or external services. Entities are tested in isolation.

rules.name: No Circular Dependencies
rules.instruction: No import cycles between packages. If two packages need each other, extract a shared interface into a third package or invert the dependency.

rules.name: Screaming Architecture
rules.instruction: Package and directory names reflect business concepts (orders, users, payments), not technical roles (models, controllers, services). The structure screams the domain.
